meta.name: KisanGPT crop-stress knowledge base
meta.notes: Every fact rendered by diagnosis_engine.py comes from this file or from the model output. Severity is computed from severity_rules below (numeric operators), never guessed.

healthy.description: Crop is within normal agronomic ranges; no stress signature detected.
actions: Continue the current irrigation and nutrition schedule
Scout the field weekly for early signs of stress
Keep records of weather and input applications
healthy.escalation: Consult the local agricultural officer if symptoms appear in more than one patch of the field.

water_stress.description: Water deficit (drought or uneven irrigation) is limiting plant growth.
actions: Irrigate early morning to a soil depth of 10-15cm
Reduce irrigation spacing to match the moisture deficit
Mulch around the base to retain soil moisture
Re-check soil moisture after 48 hours
water_stress.escalation: If soil moisture stays below 15% for more than 5 days, or wilting persists overnight, consult the local agricultural officer.

nutrient_stress.description: Nutrient imbalance or deficiency (nitrogen, micronutrients) or soil pH outside the uptake range.
visual_symptoms: yellowing between or along older leaves
purpling or browning of leaf margins
poor tillering or small new leaves
actions: Get a soil test before applying fertilizer
Correct soil pH with lime (acidic) or gypsum (alkaline) as advised
Apply a balanced N-K feed in split doses, not as a single heavy application
Ensure soil moisture is adequate when feeding
nutrient_stress.escalation: If yellowing spreads to the newest leaves or covers more than 40% of the canopy after one corrective feed, consult the local agricultural officer.

disease_stress.description: Fungal or bacterial infection causing leaf lesions and spread under humid conditions.
actions: Apply a recommended fungicide (for blast, tricyclazole-based) within 48 hours
Remove and destroy heavily infected leaves
Improve air circulation by spacing and weed control
Avoid overhead irrigation; water at the base in the morning
Monitor neighbouring plants daily for spread
disease_stress.escalation: If more than 30% of the field is affected, or lesions keep spreading after two sprays, consult the local agricultural officer.

pest_stress.description: Insect or mite feeding damage is the dominant stress.

favorable_conditions.temperature: warm, dry spells favour many pests

actions: Scout 10 plants per zone to confirm pest type and count
Install yellow sticky traps to monitor flight activity
Use a targeted, locally registered insecticide only above threshold
Encourage natural enemies; keep field borders flowering
Remove and destroy heavily infested plants
pest_stress.escalation: If more than 20% of plants show active feeding or counts keep rising after two treatments, consult the local agricultural officer.

stress_generic.description: Stress detected but the signature does not match a single named cause; treat as an undifferentiated stress signal requiring field inspection.
visual_symptoms: no clear lesion, pest or wilting pattern

favorable_conditions.note: mixed or borderline conditions; no single driver dominates

actions: Walk the field and note which symptom dominates: wilting, yellowing, lesions or chewing
Check soil moisture and recent weather against the ranges above
Take photos of the worst and the average plant for comparison
Re-run the diagnosis after 3 days, or after collecting a soil test
stress_generic.escalation: If symptoms worsen within 3 days or affect more than 25% of the field, consult the local agricultural officer.
